patch.intake_q1: Hello, I am Priya, your guide to the Hyundai CRETA. Tell me what matters to you, or say show me around to begin.

lines.text: The guide lists regular petrol, diesel and turbo petrol engines. Each uses four cylinders. Gearbox choices depend on the engine, so compare the full configuration.
Roof equipment depends on the trim. The voice-enabled panoramic roof is listed on SX, SX Premium, King, King Knight and Lounge Edition.
The regular petrol is rated at 115 PS at 6,300 revolutions per minute. It pairs with a six-speed manual or an IVT automatic.
S(O) has black alloy wheels. SX and SX Premium have diamond-cut alloys. Confirm the wheel finish against your chosen trim.
Rear-seat recline is a two-step adjustment on select trims. It is separate from the sixty-forty split, so check whether recline is included in your chosen version.
Hill-start assist helps prevent backward rolling on a slope. Driver-assistance systems do not replace safe and attentive driving.
EX, EX(O), S(O) and S(O) Knight have an eight-inch touchscreen. SX upwards use a 10.25-inch navigation display. Lounge Edition also has an 11.6-inch rear entertainment screen on the passenger side.
The guide lists the Bose eight-speaker system with a subwoofer on SX Premium, King, King Knight and Lounge Edition.
The listed fuel tank capacity is fifty litres. That alone does not establish how far the car will travel on a tank; I cannot confirm fuel-efficiency figures from these approved facts.
Front-seat ventilation is listed on SX Premium, King, King Knight and Lounge Edition. The wireless charger also appears on SX, and works only with compatible smartphones.
Up to seven years of extended warranty is listed for petrol versions only and is separately paid. Ask the dealer to confirm its coverage, exclusions and price in writing.
Six airbags are standard across the variants. The panoramic roof is available on specified trims.
Regular petrol, diesel and turbo petrol have different gearbox pairings. Compare the complete configuration before choosing.
